definition: In this context, sociometry refers to a group-therapy tradition used for warm-up and team-building exercises. It helps group members connect with one another before moving into deeper listening and sharing.

reasons: The packet only supports that the treatment uses exercises from the psychodrama/sociometry traditions as warm-up, team-building activities; it does not define sociometry itself as a group-therapy tradition.
The added claim that sociometry helps group members connect before deeper listening and sharing is an extrapolation from the article’s staged treatment sequence, not a stated definition of the term.

The packet supports that “warm-up team-building activities such as exercises from the improv and psychodrama/sociometry traditions” are used as change agents, but it does not explicitly define sociometry as a way to “help group members connect with one another before moving into deeper listening and sharing.”
The definition’s “In this context” framing is supported generally by the warm-up sequence, but the specific claimed function (“connect with one another”) is not stated in the packet.
